page.layout: One column of running text, set as verse. Above it a running head ornament; below, a centred heading and subheading. Page number top right. Two poems separated by a rule; the second has its own heading. Signatures at the foot right of the second poem. No margin notes.

main_text.l: Et ferro moritur, rogóque, & vnda. G. P.
Tantáne te generis tenuit fiducia, Gallo

l.i: Vt Regi & Gallis, Guisie, iura dares?

main_text.l: Te ne etiam nostris inimicum ciuibus vltro,
Sperasti ex alto spectans haec omnia Numen,
Lenta quidem, fateor, certo sed tempore tandem
Aduentat summi vindicis ira Dei. I
nunc: atque pio satiatus sanguine nunquam
Te proprio moriens sanguine iam satia. D.

page.notes: Woodcut ornament at head of page and an ornamental initial (fleur-de-lis cartouche) beside the first stanza; the top rule of the second poem is a double rule. Text in the first poem's opening line is partly in italic with roman "Crudelíque" and "Iusto" lines; the second poem's first line has an initial T woodcut. Show-through text from the reverse page is faintly visible and not transcribed. Greek: none. Spelling "fateor" and "vltro" as printed; "Guisie" as printed.
